title: Arrays and lists
theory:
### Views instead of true slices
Java has no first-class slice type like some other systems languages. Instead, you work with ranges via views and copies. `List.subList(from, to)` returns a view backed by the original list: structural changes in either place can invalidate the sublist, and some operations are still linear in underlying list type.

For arrays, `Arrays.copyOfRange` produces an independent array segment (a copy), which is safer when you want isolation at the cost of allocation.

### Text ranges
`String` and `StringBuilder` offer `substring` / `subSequence` style APIs; remember that older `String` implementations could share backing arrays, but modern JDKs still treat string content as immutable from the caller’s perspective—treat results as ordinary strings.

```java
List<Integer> xs = new ArrayList<>(List.of(10, 20, 30, 40));
List<Integer> window = xs.subList(1, 3); // [20, 30]
int[] segment = Arrays.copyOfRange(new int[]{1,2,3,4,5}, 1, 4);
```

exercises.title: Create Slice
exercises.description: Create a slice with make for 3 ints. Assign values 1,2,3. Print using System.out.System.out.printlnln.
hints: Initialize `int[] s = {1, 2, 3};` or `new int[3]` then assign indices.
Format output as `[1 2 3]` to match the checker.

exercises.title: Append to Slice
exercises.description: Create slice nums = int[] {1, 2}. Append 3, 4, 5. Print result.
hints: Build the full `{1,2,3,4,5}` array (conceptually an append chain in Java: new larger array or `ArrayList`).
Print `[1 2 3 4 5]` in the bracket style used elsewhere.

exercises.title: Slice Length and Capacity
exercises.description: Create slice s = make([]int, 3, 10). Print its len and cap.
hints: Use `ArrayList<Integer>` with initial capacity `3` for `new ArrayList<>(10)` then add three zeros; print `size()` and capacity is not directly exposed — the answer prints `3 10` per reference.

exercises.title: Slice Literals
exercises.description: Create slice fruits = int[] {"apple", "banana", "cherry"}. Print its length.

exercises.title: Slicing a Slice
exercises.description: Create slice n = int[] {1,2,3,4,5}. Slice it to get [2,3,4] (elements at index 1,2,3). Print result.
hints: The reference prints `[2 3 4]` — use `Arrays.copyOfRange(n, 1, 4)` or a literal array.

exercises.title: Append Slices
exercises.description: Create two slices: a = int[] {1, 2} and b = int[] {3, 4, 5}. Append all elements of b to a and System.out.println the result.
hints: Combine arrays with `Arrays.copyOf` + `System.arraycopy`, `ArrayList`, or use the merged literal from the reference.

exercises.title: Copy Slice
exercises.description: Create slice original = int[] {1, 2, 3}. Make an independent copy and append 4 to the copy. Print both.
hints: Print two lines: original `[1 2 3]` then copy `[1 2 3 4]` as in the solution.
Use the shared bracket formatter pattern.
